tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what LTEngine is: a free, open-source, self-hosted machine translation API powered by local LLMs via llama.cpp. It is fully compatible with the LibreTranslate API, meaning any client or binding that works with LibreTranslate also works with LTEngine. The README covers build requirements, supported accelerators (CUDA, Metal, Vulkan), available models, usage examples, and the project roadmap.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The main.rs file is the heart of the application. It sets up the Actix-web HTTP server, defines CLI arguments for model selection and server configuration, declares request/response DTOs, and registers all API endpoints including /translate, /languages, and /detect. This is where the LibreTranslate-compatible REST API comes to life.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's async runtime (powered by Tokio via Actix-web) allows the server to handle concurrent HTTP requests. The main function typically uses #[actix_web::main] to enter the async runtime, then binds routes to handler functions using App::new().service().

tour.title: API Error Responses
tour.description: Before diving into business logic, understand how errors are communicated. The error_response module defines a custom Actix-web error type that standardizes error formatting across all endpoints. This ensures clients receive consistent JSON error bodies regardless of which handler fails.
tour.languageLesson: In Rust, custom error types typically implement the ResponseError trait from actix-web. This trait defines how the error is converted into an HTTP response, including status code and body format, enabling ergonomic use of the ? operator in handler functions.

tour.title: Model Loading
tour.description: The models module defines how LLM weights are sourced. It supports loading from a local file path or downloading from HuggingFace remotely. This abstraction lets users either bring their own .gguf model or let LTEngine fetch one of the pre-configured Gemma3 variants automatically.
tour.languageLesson: Rust enums with associated data are ideal for modeling mutually exclusive choices like ModelSource::Local(PathBuf) versus ModelSource::Remote(String). Pattern matching on these variants at the call site makes all branches explicit and compiler-checked.

tour.title: LLM Inference Engine
tour.description: The llm module wraps the llama.cpp bindings to load the GGUF model into memory and run inference. This is the engine room: it takes a structured prompt, feeds it to the loaded LLM, and streams back generated tokens that form the translated output. GPU acceleration (CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) is handled at this layer.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's ownership model is critical when wrapping C++ libraries like llama.cpp via FFI. The LlamaContext and other native handles must be managed carefully, often wrapped in structs that implement Drop to ensure native resources are freed deterministically when they go out of scope.

tour.title: OpenAI-Compatible API Wrapper
tour.description: The llm_api module provides an OpenAI-compatible API wrapper around the core LLM inference engine. It defines request/response types matching the OpenAI chat completions format, enabling integration with existing OpenAI client libraries and tools.
tour.languageLesson: Rust structs with serde derive macros enable seamless JSON serialization/deserialization. The #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] attributes automatically implement the traits needed for JSON API request/response handling, making it easy to build compatible APIs.

tour.title: Prompt Engineering
tour.description: Translation quality depends heavily on how the prompt is structured. The prompt module builds formatted prompts for the LLM, supporting both plain text and HTML input formats. It injects source and target language codes into a template that instructs the model to act as a professional translator.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's builder pattern, implemented via a PromptBuilder struct with chainable methods, provides a fluent API for constructing complex prompts. Each method returns self, allowing calls like PromptBuilder::new().source('en').target('es').text('Hello').build().

tour.title: Language Detection
tour.description: When the source language is set to auto, the languages module steps in. It defines the supported language list and uses the lingua library to detect the input language with confidence scoring. This enables the auto-detection feature shown in the README example where Ciao! is identified as Italian.
tour.languageLesson: The lingua crate provides statistical language detection without requiring external model downloads at runtime. It works by analyzing character n-gram frequencies, making it lightweight compared to neural detection approaches while still achieving high accuracy for longer texts.

tour.title: Frontend Web Interface
tour.description: LTEngine ships with a built-in web UI for interactive translation. The frontend is a Vue.js 2 single-page application served from static files. The HTML page bootstraps the Vue app, which handles language selection, text input, file translation, dark mode toggling, and API documentation examples directly in the browser.
tour.languageLesson: Vue.js 2 uses a reactive data model where changes to the data object automatically update the DOM. The app.js file likely defines a new Vue({ el: "#app", data: { ... } }) instance with methods for calling the /translate endpoint via fetch() and updating the UI reactively.

tour.title: Static Asset Embedding
tour.description: The build.rs script is a Rust build script that runs at compile time. It uses the static-files crate to embed all frontend assets, including HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and fonts, directly into the compiled binary. This means the ltegine executable is self-contained and serves its own web UI without external file dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: Rust build scripts (build.rs) run before the main compilation and can generate code or embed resources. The include_str! and include_bytes! macros compile file contents into the binary at build time, while crates like static-files automate this for entire directories.

tour.title: Build Configuration and CI
tour.description: The Cargo.toml manifests define the Rust workspace, crate dependencies, and optional GPU features (cuda, metal, vulkan). The root workspace coordinates shared dependencies, while the ltengine crate manifest pins actix-web, llama-cpp-bindings, and serde. The GitHub Actions workflow automates release builds and artifact uploads on every push.
tour.languageLesson: Rust workspaces allow multiple crates to share a single Cargo.lock and target directory. Optional features in Cargo.toml (like cuda = ["llama-cpp-bindings/cuda"]) enable conditional compilation, letting users build with only the GPU backends they need, reducing compile time and binary size.
